correctness.rationale: For every \(m,n\ge2\), initial unseen cells form the Cartesian product of unused row and column sets. Each observed vertex sees exactly \(0\), \(p\), or \(q\) unseen neighbors where \(p,q\) are empty-support counts, so \(p,q\ge2\) prevents any forcing, while \(p=1\) or \(q=1\) permits simultaneous completion. This proves the full membership equivalence without finite-case assumptions. Exact row/column-support inclusion-exclusion yields the all-set polynomial. For inclusion-minimal sets, deletion must break each currently true threshold; this yields the row-singleton, column-singleton, and square partial-permutation cases and no others. Surjection/Stirling counts and overlap subtraction produce the stated spectra and sharp upper bound. Direct adjacency/propagation code exhaustively checks 107,654 nonempty selections on the nine boards with both dimensions from two through four, and the three-by-five board, all polynomial coefficients, and all inclusion-minimal sets. No large-parameter statement relies solely on computation.

originality.rationale: The scalar minimum in Soh–Koh 2014 is prior. The evaluated full power-domination polynomial, complete inclusion-minimal classification/count and unbounded upper-to-lower minimal spectrum are not stated or implied as enumerative claims in the inspected primary sources; original support criterion is essential to their derivation. The same-graph Mertens rook polynomial concerns ordinary domination, not propagation; general power-domination polynomial and graph-product papers lack the present family-specific formulas. An inaccessible complete version of the 2014 original remains a specific originality risk, acknowledged without treating a nonhit as proof.
residual_risks: The entire 2014 Soh–Koh five-page original was unavailable for full reading; a less prominently indexed remark might address all-set structure, though the visible lemmas and Theorem 3.3 address minimum number only.
Other pre-2018 theses, instructional treatments, or alternate rook/line-graph/PMU terminology may contain an equivalent enumeration not surfaced by the searches.

The inclusion-exclusion counting machinery is standard and appears for ordinary rook domination; originality rests on the new power-forcing support criterion and exact deletion-minimal classification, not on inclusion-exclusion as a method.

value.rationale: A natural two-parameter Cartesian-product family now has an exact count at every feasible sensor-set cardinality and a complete combinatorial classification of irreducible layouts, not merely the previously known optimal cardinality. Rectangular \(3\times n\) boards exhibit irreducible layouts with \(n-1\) sensors despite optimal size two, an unbounded and operationally motivated distinction. The contrast with squares, where all minimal layouts have one fixed size, is a sharp structural boundary. The work is complete for every \(m,n\ge2\) and has self-contained mathematical value independent of downstream applications.
